title: Concrete error reduction by majority
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model closed under majority, and let $L$ be a language with an efficient verifier $M_0$ using $a_0(n+1)^{k_0}$ random bits, whose acceptance probability on members and rejection probability on nonmembers are each at least $2/3$. For any natural numbers $b,e$, there is an efficient verifier $M$ whose acceptance probability on members and rejection probability on nonmembers are each at least $1-(1/2)^{b(n+1)^e}$, using $(18b+18)a_0(n+1)^{e+k_0}$ random bits on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $M_0$ has acceptance and rejection probabilities at least $2/3$ on the respective inputs
